proof_summary: Solving the continued-fraction recurrence gives \(A(n)=P/\gcd(P,2(n-1)(n-3)!)\), where \(P=n^2+2n-4\); quadratic reciprocity makes \(5\) a square modulo \(p\), so choosing \(n\equiv\sqrt5-1\pmod p\) yields \(P=pm\). Since \(n<p\), \(p\) is coprime to the factorial factor, while bounds show \(m\le n-3\) and hence \(m\mid(n-3)!\), so the gcd is exactly \(m\); the small exceptional cases reduce directly to \(p=11\).
